examples.trans: Our family has real noble roots.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'лучиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to happen', forming an aspectual pair with 'случаться'.

examples.text: Скажите, а что случилось с вашим лицом?
examples.trans: Tell me, what happened to your face?

examples.text: Скажи мне честно, у тебя что-то случилось?
examples.trans: Tell me honestly, did something happen to you?

examples.text: А что у вас случилось перед началом?
examples.trans: And what happened with you before the start?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in front of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Буду каждое утро плакать перед зеркалом.
examples.trans: I will cry every morning in front of the mirror.

examples.text: Мы красиво загримируем вас перед выходом в зал.
examples.trans: We will put stage makeup on you nicely before you go out into the hall.

examples.text: А что у вас случилось перед началом?
examples.trans: And what happened with you before the start?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'beginning', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: А что у вас случилось перед началом?
examples.trans: And what happened with you before the start?

examples.text: Это только начало.
examples.trans: It's only the beginning.

examples.text: В начале недели.
examples.trans: At the beginning of the week.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я не могу пойти против воли папы.
examples.trans: I cannot go against my dad's will.

examples.text: Ты можешь сразу строго его отшить?
examples.trans: Can you brush him off strictly right away?

examples.text: Ну конечно, дочка, могла даже не просить!
examples.trans: Well of course, daughter, you did not even have to ask!

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (root 'звониться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to get through', forming an aspectual pair with 'дозваниваться'.

examples.text: Я не могу дозвониться, и гроб пропал!
examples.trans: I cannot reach him by phone, and the coffin has disappeared!

examples.text: Я не могу дозвониться до своей жены.
examples.trans: I cannot get through to my wife.

examples.text: Дома не могу ему дозвониться.
examples.trans: At home I can't reach him.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'coffin', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Подожди, кого ты выпустишь из этого гроба?
examples.trans: Wait, who will you release from this coffin?

examples.text: Нет, ребята, в гроб я не полезу!
examples.trans: No, guys, I am not climbing into a coffin!

examples.text: Почему этот гроб вдруг стал таким тяжёлым?
examples.trans: Why did this coffin suddenly become so heavy?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (root 'пасть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to disappear'.

examples.text: Я не могу дозвониться, и гроб пропал!
examples.trans: I cannot reach him by phone, and the coffin has disappeared!

examples.text: Да вы что? Как мог пропасть гроб?
examples.trans: You don't say? How could a coffin disappear?

examples.text: Самсонов пропал.
examples.trans: Samsonov is missing.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('yes') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лёва, да ты просто настоящий зодчий!
examples.trans: Lyova, you are simply a true master builder!

examples.text: Да вы что? Как мог пропасть гроб?
examples.trans: You don't say? How could a coffin disappear?

examples.text: Да ну?
examples.trans: Oh yeah?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.

examples.text: Сплю точно как бурый медведь зимой в берлоге!
examples.trans: I sleep just like a brown bear in its den in winter!

examples.text: Как жалко, что Вика не ведёт корпоративы!
examples.trans: What a pity that Vika does not host corporate parties!

examples.text: Мы оденем вас как настоящего графа Дракулу!
examples.trans: We will dress you up like the real Count Dracula!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'soon'.

examples.text: Но скоро у нас важный корпоратив банка!
examples.trans: But soon we have an important bank corporate party!

examples.text: Скоро выход Дракулы, а у нас катастрофа!
examples.trans: Dracula's entrance is soon, and we have a catastrophe!

examples.text: Держитесь, Дмитрий Владимирович, мы вас скоро откроем!
examples.trans: Hang on, Dmitry Vladimirovich, we will open you up soon!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'exit', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Мы красиво загримируем вас перед выходом в зал.
examples.trans: We will put stage makeup on you nicely before you go out into the hall.

examples.text: Скоро выход Дракулы, а у нас катастрофа!
examples.trans: Dracula's entrance is soon, and we have a catastrophe!

examples.text: Выход всегда есть.
examples.trans: There's always a way out.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'soon', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Скоро выход Дракулы, а у нас катастрофа!
examples.trans: Dracula's entrance is soon, and we have a catastrophe!

examples.text: Это мои любимые итальянские мокасины, не трогай!
examples.trans: Those are my favorite Italian moccasins, do not touch!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('we') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Ничего, мы будем брать крепость измором!
examples.trans: Never mind, we will take the fortress by attrition!

examples.text: Мой отец против того, чтобы мы встречались.
examples.trans: My father is against the two of us dating.

examples.text: Без его согласия у нас ничего не решается.
examples.trans: Without his consent nothing is decided in our family.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'catastrophe', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Скоро выход Дракулы, а у нас катастрофа!
examples.trans: Dracula's entrance is soon, and we have a catastrophe!

examples.text: Это просто катастрофа для нас!
examples.trans: This is simply a catastrophe for us!

examples.text: Это просто катастрофа для нашей кампании!
examples.trans: This is simply a catastrophe for our campaign!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'guys', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: У меня большая беда с лицом, ребята.
examples.trans: I have a big disaster with my face, guys.

examples.text: А я сейчас тихо пойду спать, ребята.
examples.trans: And I am quietly going to go to sleep right now, guys.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, пока все свободны, идите работать!
examples.trans: All right, guys, everyone is dismissed for now, go work!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'immediately'.

examples.text: Немедленно отстань от меня со своей игрушкой!
examples.trans: Leave me alone immediately with your toy!

examples.text: Всё, Вика, я тебя немедленно увольняю отсюда!
examples.trans: That is it, Vika, I am firing you from here immediately!

examples.text: Отпустить немедленно!
examples.trans: Release him immediately!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'foolish', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Это дурацкий вопрос.
examples.trans: This is a foolish question.

examples.text: У него дурацкие шутки.
examples.trans: He makes silly jokes.

examples.text: Эта дурацкая рыба — как плохой знак.
examples.trans: This foolish fish is like a bad sign.
